claims.text: Local lattice distortions in high-entropy alloys create heterogeneous stress fields that act as strong dislocation-pinning sites.
Emerging short-range chemical order creates heterogeneous stress fields that act as strong dislocation-pinning sites.
Dislocation pinning by lattice distortion and short-range order governs hardness and strength in high-entropy alloys.
Controlled annealing that enhances short-range order will increase hardness relative to a fully random solid-solution baseline.
Rapidly quenched equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi can provide a nearly random, single-phase solid solution with minimal short-range order.
Annealing below the disorder–order transition while permitting atomic rearrangement can promote short-range order without inducing precipitation or grain growth.
Annealing-induced short-range order develops as nanoscale chemically ordered clusters.
Nanoscale chemically ordered regions increase local lattice strain.
Nanoscale chemically ordered regions create spatially varying stress fields.
Short-range-order-induced lattice distortions create additional energy barriers to dislocation motion.
These additional energy barriers require higher applied stresses for dislocation activation.
Restricted dislocation mobility increases hardness.
Restricted dislocation mobility increases yield strength.
An annealed HEA with enhanced short-range order will have greater hardness than the as-quenched baseline.
An annealed HEA with enhanced short-range order will have greater yield strength than the as-quenched baseline.
The annealed material will exhibit a higher stress plateau in nanoindentation or in situ micro-compression testing.
The annealed material will exhibit a more pronounced stress drop associated with dislocation nucleation.
The proposed behavior is expected to apply to single-phase equiatomic or near-equiatomic HEAs when secondary phases, grain growth, and precipitation are absent.
The strengthening effect of short-range order is expected to be less pronounced when inherent lattice mismatch is very low.
The quantitative contribution of short-range order to hardness and strength varies with composition and annealing parameters.
